Two relations are available.

  corpus      one row per document in the working sample, WITH the text.
  corpus_meta one row per document in the whole corpus, WITHOUT the text.

Columns (identical in both, except `text`, which only `corpus` has):
  id                    document identifier
  text                  document text (corpus only)
  url, domain           source URL and its host
  dump, date            crawl the document came from, and its timestamp
  language              language label assigned by the corpus pipeline
  language_score        the pipeline's confidence in that label
  minhash_cluster_size  size of the near-duplicate cluster the document
                        represented before deduplication (1 = unique)
  fasttext, langdetect  labels from two independent off-the-shelf language
                        identifiers, shipped with the corpus release
  lingua_top            top language from a third identifier, which reports
                        a distribution over languages within the document
  lingua_top_p          that identifier's proportion for lingua_top
  n_bad_words           number of profanity-list matches recorded by the
                        corpus release
  n_chars, n_words, n_lines  document size
Raw pipeline fields `top_langs` (JSON) and `lingua` (list of
(language, proportion) pairs, as text) are also available on both
relations if you want the full distributions.

Táto práca sa zaoberá prostriedkami na analýzu bezpečnostných protokolov. V úvode sú popísané požiadavky na bezpečnostné protokoly spoločne s možnosťami útokov na ne. Následne sú spomenuté základné techniky, špecifikačné jazyky a nástroje používané na formálnu verifikáciu protokolov. Ďalšia časť obsahuje popis najznámejších protokolov spoločne s ich neformálnymi zápismi. V práci sú spomenuté viaceré medzinárodné hodnotiace štandardy používané v oblasti informačných technológií. Záver práce obsahuje detailnejší popis dvoch vybraných nástrojov (AVISPA, Scyther). Tieto nástroje a ich výstupy sú porovnané podľa navrhnutej metodiky.This thesis is focused on tools which are used to analyzed security protocols. In the beginning of the thesis key goals of security protocols are mentioned and also basic attacks on them are illustrated. Subsequently basic verification techniques, specification languages and verification tools are described. Next part of thesis contains description of protocols in common syntax. Then the main standards used for evaluation of information security products are mentioned. In the end of thesis two well-known verification tools – AVISPA and Scyther - are described and compared to designed methodology of comparing verification tools and their outputs.

input.description: A large-scale, machine-generated content-farm/SEO-spam network is hosted on randomly-named subdomains of Google's free Firebase hosting (*.firebaseapp.com, *.web.app). Each subdomain name is a Slovak or Scandinavian finance/get-rich-quick keyword (e.g. "akozbohatnut" = how to get rich, "investerarpengar" = Swedish "invest money", "pracovnemiesta" = job vacancies, "danove" = taxes, "nakupzlata" = buy gold) plus a random letter suffix, and each hosts thousands of pages of incoherent, multi-topic text stitched together from scraped fragments (finance/crypto glossary snippets, news snippets, unrelated Q&A, sometimes switching mid-document into Czech, Bosnian/Serbian, or Slovenian). The pages are not authored prose and are not really "Slovak documents" in the intended sense, despite passing the language filter with high average confidence (0.98) and evading near-duplicate dedup entirely (avg minhash_cluster_size ≈ 1, since every domain/page uses a unique random suffix/URL).
input.evidence: Domain-level aggregation shows domain LIKE '%.firebaseapp.com' OR '%.web.app' covers 1,408,437 documents (5.32% of the 26.47M-doc corpus), spread across thousands of distinct randomly-suffixed subdomains (e.g. akoinvestovatffsq, akozbohatnuthdiy, pracovnemiestakulp, nakupzlatafvvi, each with ~2,400-2,650 docs, share_of_domain=1.0). Inspected 32 sampled documents (evaluate_detector, seeds 13 and 99): all were incoherent multi-topic scrapes (crypto/finance glossary text abruptly followed by unrelated topics like Simpsons characters, dog food, football results, cat behavior), several with sentences in other Slavic languages (Bosnian/Serbian, Slovenian) interleaved. minhash_cluster_size is ~1 for essentially all of them (avg 1.002) despite the content clearly being templated/recombined across the network, meaning the dedup step entirely misses this network because each page's exact text differs. language_score for the domain averages 0.98, i.e. the langID pipeline is confidently fooled. No counter-examples found among the 32 inspected (no genuine small personal/business Slovak blogs on Firebase hosting turned up in-sample), though it is possible a small minority of genuine sites use this hosting and would be wrongly caught.
input.likely_false_positives: A genuine small Slovak personal or hobby site legitimately hosted on Firebase (free Google hosting is popular for small apps/blogs) would be wrongly caught; none were observed in ~32 inspected documents, but the selector cannot distinguish them from the farm by domain pattern alone.
input.assertion: A clean corpus should exclude or down-weight documents from this content-farm network; at minimum, minhash-based deduplication should be enhanced with a near-template/boilerplate detector so this kind of shallowly-varied spam is not treated as unique high-value text.

input.description: A second, separate spam network of thousands of randomly-named domains (English dictionary-word-like names + generic gTLDs/ccTLDs such as .com/.me/.fr/.bike/.online/.info/.nl/.it/.us/.br) hosts keyword-stuffed, incoherent "word salad" adult/porn doorway pages that are grammatically broken pastiches of scraped Slovak sentence fragments and tag lists, not genuine documents. Many share a literal CMS template header "Posted by Admin | in <Month> <Day>, 2020 |".
input.selector: n_bad_words >= 3 AND domain NOT LIKE '%.sk' AND domain NOT LIKE '%.cz'
input.evidence: domain_stats on n_bad_words>=3 shows dozens of domains (slovhubkia.com, adv-moto-girl.bike, baazzaa.com, aaronpowell.me, alexpichel.com, bananapepper.fr, accesslocator.net/.org/.info, agencerepublique.me/.net, and many more) each contributing 1,000-6,000 docs with 75-92% of their own documents matching high bad-word counts. Inspected 32 documents total via evaluate_detector (seeds 11 and 42): 32/32 were confirmed word-salad porn/dating spam pages — grammatically incoherent strings of scraped fragments/tag lists about explicit content, all with random-looking domain names unrelated to Slovakia, minhash_cluster_size mostly 1 (unique per page despite templated structure). A follow-up sample of the same domains without the bad-word filter (e.g. bananapepper.fr) showed the identical word-salad template style even at n_bad_words=0, meaning the true farm is larger than what this conservative selector catches. The regexp literal 'Posted by Admin \\| in [A-Za-z]+ \\d+, 2020' alone matches an estimated 28,592 docs (0.108%) and also had 12/12 precision when checked independently.
input.likely_false_positives: A genuine Slovak site on a non-.sk/.cz domain (e.g. a Slovak business using a .com or .eu domain) that legitimately discusses adult/medical topics or uses informal/profane language (e.g. forum arguments) could be wrongly caught by the bad-word threshold; this is why the domain-diversity check (thousands of distinct low-traffic domains, each ~70-90% flagged) was used as corroborating evidence rather than relying on word count alone.
input.assertion: A clean corpus should not contain incoherent keyword-stuffed doorway pages; documents matching this template/domain signature should be filtered as spam regardless of the language-ID confidence assigned to them.

## Summary

I audited the Slovak (`slk_Latn`) slice of the
corpus (26.47M documents, corpus_meta) using aggregate SQL, domain statistics, and targeted document inspection (used
~197 of 300 inspection budget). Two systematic, high-prevalence defects were found, quantified, and recorded as machine-checkable findings; several other hypotheses were invest

igated and rejected or judged too weak to record.

### Findings recorded

**1. `firebase_content_farm_spam` — 5.32% of the corpus (1,408,437

docs)**
A large content-farm/SEO-spam network hosted on randomly-suffixed `*.firebaseapp.com`/`*.web.app` subdomains (e.g. `akoz
bohatnut<random>`, `investerarpengar<random>`, `pracovnem
iesta<random>` — Slovak/Swedish "get rich quick"/"invest money"/"jobs" keywords + random letters). P
ages are incoherent multi-topic scrapes stitched from unrelated fragments (finance/crypto glossaries, news snippets, Sim
psons trivia, pet care, sometimes switching mid-page into Bosnian/Serbian or Slovenian). Desp
ite this, the language filter is fooled with high confidence (avg `language_score` 0.98) and dedup is defeated entirely (avg
`minhash_cluster_size` ≈ 1, since every page/domain is uniquely randomized). Verified against 32 inspected documents, all positive. Selector: `

domain LIKE '%.firebaseapp.com' OR domain LIKE '%.web.app'` — exact on full corpus.

**2. `porn_spam_keyword_farm` — 0.36% of the corpus

(94,946 docs, conservative floor)**
A second spam network of thousands of randomly-named domains (dictionary-word names
+ generic TLDs like `.me/.fr/.bike/.online/.info/.com`) hosting keyword-stuffed, ungrammatical "word
salad" adult-content doorway pages, many sharing a literal template header `"Posted by Admin | in
<Month> <Day>, 2020 |"`. Verified against 32+12 inspected documents, all positive (100% precision in-sample). This undercounts the true farm size
— the same domains also produce non-explicit word-salad pages that don't trip the bad-word count.

Selector: `n_bad_words >= 3 AND domain NOT LIKE '%.sk' AND domain NOT LIKE '%.cz'` — exact on full corpus.

Together these two networ
ks alone account for **~5.68% of the entire corpus** — a large, systematic contamination that inflates document count with non-authored

, non-representative "Slovak" text.

### Hypotheses investigated and rejected/deprioritized
- **Weird `lingua_top
` labels (sw, st, sn, so, eu, tl, la) on short informal text**: checked — these are genuine, col
loquial Slovak forum posts that a distributional LID misfires on due to short/informal input. Not a corpus defect,

just LID noise on legitimate text.
- **`fasttext='cs'` documents labeled `slk`** (~1.6
% of corpus): mostly genuine Slovak text with borrowed Czech words/phrases (e-shops
quoting Czech manufacturer copy, Slovak-Czech medical Q&A sites, Czech university thesis abstracts written by Slovak students —
where the Slovak abstract itself is the majority of characters). Not a coherent single defect; the clearly bad inst
ances (kamsi.sk/svetomatika.ru-style spun bilingual S

EO text) were a small, non-dominant slice and didn't merit a separate finding from the two above.
- **All
-three-LID-agree-`cs`** (44,251 docs, 0.17%): spread thinly across many small domains with

no dominant single cause; rejected as too diffuse to write a precise, high-precision selector for.
- **sk.air
bnb.com template-heavy listings** (136K docs): mostly UI boilerplate ("Superhostiteľ
", "Celý objekt"...) around host-written descriptions in other languages; only ~6
% have non-Slovak `lingua_top`, so the doc-level language label is largely still defensible. Real but weak — did

## Summary

I audited the Slovak (`slk_Latn`) slice of the corpus (26.47M documents, corpus_meta) using aggregate SQL, domain statistics, and targeted document inspection (used ~197 of 300 inspection budget). Two systematic, high-prevalence defects were found, quantified, and recorded as machine-checkable findings; several other hypotheses were investigated and rejected or judged too weak to record.

### Findings recorded

**1. `firebase_content_farm_spam` — 5.32% of the corpus (1,408,437 docs)**
A large content-farm/SEO-spam network hosted on randomly-suffixed `*.firebaseapp.com`/`*.web.app` subdomains (e.g. `akozbohatnut<random>`, `investerarpengar<random>`, `pracovnemiesta<random>` — Slovak/Swedish "get rich quick"/"invest money"/"jobs" keywords + random letters). Pages are incoherent multi-topic scrapes stitched from unrelated fragments (finance/crypto glossaries, news snippets, Simpsons trivia, pet care, sometimes switching mid-page into Bosnian/Serbian or Slovenian). Despite this, the language filter is fooled with high confidence (avg `language_score` 0.98) and dedup is defeated entirely (avg `minhash_cluster_size` ≈ 1, since every page/domain is uniquely randomized). Verified against 32 inspected documents, all positive. Selector: `domain LIKE '%.firebaseapp.com' OR domain LIKE '%.web.app'` — exact on full corpus.

**2. `porn_spam_keyword_farm` — 0.36% of the corpus (94,946 docs, conservative floor)**
A second spam network of thousands of randomly-named domains (dictionary-word names + generic TLDs like `.me/.fr/.bike/.online/.info/.com`) hosting keyword-stuffed, ungrammatical "word salad" adult-content doorway pages, many sharing a literal template header `"Posted by Admin | in <Month> <Day>, 2020 |"`. Verified against 32+12 inspected documents, all positive (100% precision in-sample). This undercounts the true farm size — the same domains also produce non-explicit word-salad pages that don't trip the bad-word count. Selector: `n_bad_words >= 3 AND domain NOT LIKE '%.sk' AND domain NOT LIKE '%.cz'` — exact on full corpus.

Together these two networks alone account for **~5.68% of the entire corpus** — a large, systematic contamination that inflates document count with non-authored, non-representative "Slovak" text.

### Hypotheses investigated and rejected/deprioritized
- **Weird `lingua_top` labels (sw, st, sn, so, eu, tl, la) on short informal text**: checked — these are genuine, colloquial Slovak forum posts that a distributional LID misfires on due to short/informal input. Not a corpus defect, just LID noise on legitimate text.
- **`fasttext='cs'` documents labeled `slk`** (~1.6% of corpus): mostly genuine Slovak text with borrowed Czech words/phrases (e-shops quoting Czech manufacturer copy, Slovak-Czech medical Q&A sites, Czech university thesis abstracts written by Slovak students — where the Slovak abstract itself is the majority of characters). Not a coherent single defect; the clearly bad instances (kamsi.sk/svetomatika.ru-style spun bilingual SEO text) were a small, non-dominant slice and didn't merit a separate finding from the two above.
- **All-three-LID-agree-`cs`** (44,251 docs, 0.17%): spread thinly across many small domains with no dominant single cause; rejected as too diffuse to write a precise, high-precision selector for.
- **sk.airbnb.com template-heavy listings** (136K docs): mostly UI boilerplate ("Superhostiteľ", "Celý objekt"...) around host-written descriptions in other languages; only ~6% have non-Slovak `lingua_top`, so the doc-level language label is largely still defensible. Real but weak — didn't record.
- **Short documents (<30 words)**: negligible (16 docs total) — rejected.
- **Duplicate URLs across crawls** (1.4M URLs seen >1×): expected behavior for recrawled homepages/listings with changing content, not a dedup failure — rejected.
- **Large `minhash_cluster_size` representative docs** (cookie banners, loan-scam landing pages): correctly collapsed to one representative per cluster by the existing dedup step — not a residual defect in the delivered corpus.
- **CSRF-error-page boilerplate fragment glued onto product pages**: real but small (~0.09%) and not really a language/content defect — skipped.

### What I'd investigate with more budget
- Build a broader, precision-checked selector for the porn-spam farm that doesn't rely on `n_bad_words` (e.g. a text-shape heuristic for incoherent tag-list/fragment-concatenation structure), since the current selector likely underestimates true farm size substantially.
- Characterize whether other free-hosting platforms (e.g. `*.blogspot.com`, `*.wordpress.com`, `*.github.io`) harbor similar randomized-subdomain content farms, since the Firebase pattern suggests this is a generic evasion strategy against crawls/dedup.
- Quantify the Slovak/Czech bilingual-forum phenomenon (livedoctor.cz-style) more rigorously if it turns out to be larger than the small sample here suggested.
- Investigate mid-frequency `minhash_cluster_size` (10–1000) documents for a "near-duplicate but not quite deduped" tail that could indicate templated business-directory spam distinct from the two farms found.
